import sys, json, hashlib, datetime, re

# THE HANDOVER (curator, GH #896). What one session leaves for the next, and
# what a renewed live session of the same call needs to carry on. Three lanes,
# one rule: nothing here writes the wall and nothing here decides the window --
# `./intake` and `./policy` do. This cell reads the ledger, composes ONE block,
# and puts it where it is needed.
#
#   in_close    a session closed: its turns go to `./summarizer` (the ONE model
#               door of the hive, OR-KY-62) -- off the hot path, nobody waits
#               on it -- and the answer, the note, becomes a block of kind
#               `summary` plus a `marks` row `handover` (state `prepared`). A
#               session that left no turn prepares nothing.
#   handover    `./policy` meets the first call of a session it did not serve
#               last. A NEW session (no wall row before this round) gets the
#               system leaf `history.handover`: the note prepared at the close
#               of the session served last and the topic still open, or --
#               without a close -- the topic alone, put together without a
#               model. Then the call goes back to `./policy` as `handover-done`
#               with nothing but this cell's writes: what the call reads is
#               `./policy`'s alone (review I-1 -- a copy of its reads here went
#               stale the day the window got a plan), and it reads the leaf
#               among the slots. OR-KY-U1: the first turn of a session never
#               waits on a model.
#   in_renewed  a duplex session of a running call was renewed at its limit
#               (`voice` route `renewed`): the running conversation -- the
#               newest `renew_rounds` rounds as text, the summary, pins,
#               commitments, topic -- is put together WITHOUT a model
#               (OR-KY-U3: the takeover happens mid-call) and leaves as a
#               `sidecar` section `context` that carries `renewal_n` and
#               `call_id`, which the member turns into the call's `in_advise`.
#
# The block is at most `handover_chars` long; what does not fit is cut by rank:
# pins and open commitments first, then the topic, then the latest turns, the
# summary last (review focus 5). The leaf of a new session carries no pins:
# `./policy` shows every valid pin in the same window already (`pinned.*` or
# where it arrived), and a second copy froze a pin at the close that expires
# on its own there (OR-KY.U.14). A renewed live session sees no curator system
# part at all, so its block carries them.
#
# Every step is the same loop against `./ledger`: the reads this step needs,
# named by what they read, in ONE bundle; when the answer holds every read the
# data asks for, the block is composed and written; otherwise the bundle grows
# by what the answer revealed (a pin's block, the topic's opening turn) and goes
# out again. The ids are deterministic, so "every read is there" is a set test.
#
# The topic still open (OR-KY-71): the `name` of the newest `topic` mark that
# names one, unless an `end` came after it; the mark's value is the canonical
# JSON `{"movement", "name"}` `./intake` writes from the model's `memory`
# section.
#
# Who may read what (GH #925): the round that RECEIVES decides. The note is
# written from the closing session's own words and carries the meet of their
# audiences; the leaf is for the NEW session, so every source of it -- the
# note, the topic -- passes the gate of the new session's round, and the leaf's
# audience goes to `state` `handover_audience` beside it, bound to the leaf's
# hash, which `./policy` holds against the round of every later call of the
# session, for the leaf of that hash only (review Abschluss I-1). A renewal is
# gated by the round of the renewal. Without a round only rows of the running
# session pass (OR-BD-4); a row from before the rule never does (OR-BD-5). The
# store filters first (GH #932): every gated read asks for visible rows only,
# so the renewal's `renew_rounds` window, the summaries and marks it scans and
# the size of the block hang on what the round may see -- a hidden row is not
# even counted.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
P = doc.get("params") or {}
header = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}


# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. Every ledger read asks the store
# first (`round_where`, GH #932), so a hidden row never comes back at all; the
# Python gate stays as the second line behind it.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))


def meet_of_rows(values):
    """`audience_meet` for a row written from other rows (GH #932, PP-BD-12).
    Since PP-BD-12 `[]` marks a round-less row, which round-less calls of its
    session read; an EMPTY meet is that mark only when every source that
    names no `*` is round-less itself. An empty meet of declared rounds
    ({a} and {b}, or {e,a} and a round-less row) names nobody: None, and the
    row reaches no round -- before PP-BD-12 such a `[]` reached none either."""
    out = audience_meet(values)
    if out == "[]":
        for v in values:
            c = audience_of(v)
            if c is not None and c != "[]" and "*" not in json.loads(c):
                return None
    return out



def _int(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip()):
        return default
    return int(float(v))


# The knobs. The literal beside each name is the shipped default, the same
# number `params` and `contract.settings` carry.
HANDOVER_CHARS = _int("handover_chars", 3000)
RENEW_ROUNDS = _int("renew_rounds", 12)

FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
ME = "curator-handover"
POLICY = "curator-policy"
LEAF_PATH = "history.handover"
# How many rows of the wall a renewal reads back at most: `renew_rounds` rounds
# of a tool-heavy talk are some tens of rows; the cap keeps one read bounded.
RENEW_WALL_ROWS = 600
# How many of the newest summaries a renewal reads to find the newest one its
# round may see (GH #925): one the round may not see is skipped, never used as
# a cover, so its rows are not left out of the block as an unexplained gap.
RENEW_SUMMARIES = 8
# How many `topic` marks are read to find the topic still open, and how many
# `handover` marks to find the newest prepared note.
TOPIC_MARKS = 40
HANDOVER_MARKS = 40
# A topic's name is the model's words; a longer one is cut here.
TOPIC_CHARS = 240
# Tool payloads are cut in the summarizer's transcript, never in the wall.
TRANSCRIPT_TOOL_CHARS = 2000
# The note's transcript keeps the newest lines within this many characters:
# a session of a whole day must not push the note request past what the
# summarizer takes, and fall back to no note at all (review M-7).
NOTE_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS = 60000
COMMITMENT = "commitment"
# A block's short id means something to the model behind this hive
# (`history_read` takes it) and nothing to a live voice, which would read it
# out: the block for a renewed session is said into a call, so every id leaves
# it (OR-KY-68, R-27-3) -- in every form the colony makes one (OR-KY-81,
# OR-KY-84): the window's bracket `[#<12 hex>]`, the window's forms of a
# released, a shortened and an expired block (`curator/policy` RELEASED_FORM,
# SHRUNK_FORM, EXPIRED_FORM), a parenthesised one, the bare `#<12..16 hex>` a
# history tool answers with and the full 64-digit block id. The pattern is
# `talky/splitter`'s SHORT_ID, byte for byte (OR-KY-83): code cells share no
# module, so the copies are kept equal by a test, never by hand. The
# `history.handover` leaf keeps the ids -- its reader is the curated model.
SHORT_ID = re.compile(
    r"[ \t]?(?:\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?: released[^\]\n]{0,64}| expired)?\]"
    r"|\[shortened[^\]\n#]{0,40}#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}[^\]\n]{0,4}\]"
    r"|\(#[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}\)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#(?=[0-9]{0,15}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{12,16}(?!\w)"
    r"|(?<![\w#])#?(?=[0-9]{0,63}[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{64}(?!\w))")
LEAF_HEAD = ("[where the last session left off -- session %s, %s; what was said"
             " and kept there, not what is true]")
RENEW_HEAD = ("[the call so far: this is a renewed session of the same call --"
              " carry on from here, do not greet again]")
HANDOVER_PROMPT = (
    "You write the handover note from one session with a model to the next session of the"
    " same model. You get the transcript of the session that just ended. Write down, in the"
    " order it happened, what the next session has to know to carry on: what was asked and"
    " answered, what was decided, what was promised and is still open, names and numbers as"
    " they were given. Report, do not judge: a statement is not true because it was made."
    " Leave out greetings and small talk, and any identity, persona or standing instructions"
    " of the model. Answer with the note only, in at most %d characters.")
NOTE_TITLE = "The last session, summarised:"

try:
    _MEM
except NameError:
    # A cache of this child's own writes, never the truth (`code` runner mode
    # `resident`): a restarted child starts empty and the ledger read decides.
    _MEM = {"seq": 0, "prepared": set()}


def without_ids(text):
    """The text without any block short id, deterministically (OR-KY-68)."""
    return SHORT_ID.sub("", text)


def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def short(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None -- the
    fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605), measured, never parsed."""
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()


def element_of(row):
    try:
        el = json.loads(str((row or {}).get("body") or ""))
    except Exception:
        return None
    return el if isinstance(el, dict) else None


def text_of(row):
    el = element_of(row)
    return str(el.get("text") or "") if el else ""


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)


def now_ms():
    return int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000)


def next_seq():
    """A `marks.seq`: microseconds since the epoch, strictly above anything
    this child minted before (OR-KY-61: the store has no autoincrement)."""
    base = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000000)
    base = max(base, _MEM["seq"] + 1)
    _MEM["seq"] = base
    return base


def epoch_ms(value):
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return int(t.timestamp() * 1000)


def with_audience(row, audience):
    """A row to insert, always with `audience_set`: a row written without a
    round carries `[]` (PP-BD-12), so a round-less read of its own session
    finds it by value in the store (GH #932) -- NULL is left to rows from
    before the rule, which reach no round (GH #925, OR-BD-5)."""
    row["audience_set"] = "[]" if audience is None else audience
    return row


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=""):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/handover: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def lstore(ops, phase, call="", reason="", reply=ME):
    """One message to `./ledger`. Every key the edge reads is always present
    (a failed CEL modifier skips the edge)."""
    return {"header": {"route": "lstore", "phase": phase, "reply_cell": reply,
                       "cur_call": call, "cur_reason": reason},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in ops]}


def legs(body):
    out = {}
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "error_code": ""}
    results = body.get("results")
    if isinstance(results, list):
        for r in results:
            if isinstance(r, dict):
                leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                                     {"payload": None, "error_code": ""})
                leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
    elif len(out) == 1:
        next(iter(out.values()))["error_code"] = str(hop.get("error_code") or "")
    return out


def rows(lg, cid):
    p = (lg.get(cid) or {}).get("payload")
    return p if isinstance(p, list) else []


def sel(table, columns, where=None, order=None, limit=None):
    a = {"operation": "select", "table": table, "columns": columns}
    if where:
        a["where"] = where
    if order:
        a["order_by"] = [{"col": c, "dir": o} for c, o in order]
    if limit:
        a["limit"] = limit
    return a


def ins(table, row):
    return {"operation": "insert", "table": table, "row": row}


def upd(table, values, where):
    return {"operation": "update", "table": table, "set": values, "where": where}


def loads(text, default):
    try:
        v = json.loads(text)
    except Exception:
        return default
    return v if isinstance(v, type(default)) else default


def report_errors(lg):
    for cid, leg in lg.items():
        if leg["error_code"]:
            sys.stderr.write("curator/handover: ledger op %s failed: %s\n"
                             % (cid, leg["error_code"]))


# ============================================================== PURE PARTS
def pin_valid(row, as_of_ms):
    """A pin stands until its `until` (RFC 3339) or for ever when it has
    none; an `until` that does not read as a time is taken as none."""
    until = epoch_ms(row.get("until"))
    return until is None or until > as_of_ms


def topic_move(value):
    """(movement, name) of one `topic` mark's value: the canonical JSON
    `{"movement", "name"}` (OR-KY-71), or the bare movement a ledger written
    before it holds (then without a name)."""
    text = str(value or "").strip()
    try:
        v = json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        v = None
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return (str(v.get("movement") or "").strip().lower(), str(v.get("name") or "").strip())
    return (text.lower(), "")


def open_topic(marks):
    """(name, mark) of the topic still open, or ("", None): the `name` of the
    newest `topic` mark that names one, unless an `end` came after it
    (OR-KY-71). `marks` newest first, and only those the round may see (GH
    #925); a mark without a name belongs to the topic open at the time, so an
    `end` without one closes it. The mark is the source the name came from."""
    for m in marks:
        move, name = topic_move(m.get("value"))
        if move == "end":
            return "", None
        if name:
            return name, m
    return "", None


def transcript_line(kind, el):
    text = str(el.get("text") or "")
    if kind in ("tool_call", "recall", "brief"):
        try:
            fn = json.loads(text) or {}
        except Exception:
            fn = {}
        return "assistant called %s(%s)" % (fn.get("name") or "?", fn.get("arguments") or "")
    if kind == "tool_result":
        if len(text) > TRANSCRIPT_TOOL_CHARS:
            text = text[:TRANSCRIPT_TOOL_CHARS] + " [cut]"
        return "tool result: " + text
    if kind == "assistant":
        return "assistant: " + stripped_text(text)
    if kind == "peer":
        who = str(el.get("speaker") or el.get("speaker_ref") or "")
        return ("peer %s: " % who if who else "peer: ") + text
    if kind in ("advice", "delegation"):
        return "note: " + text
    return "user: " + text


def transcript(wall, blocks):
    """The note request's transcript of a session: the newest lines within
    NOTE_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS, a marker where earlier ones were left out."""
    lines = []
    for r in wall:
        el = element_of(blocks.get(str(r.get("hash") or "")))
        if el is not None:
            lines.append((r, transcript_line(str(r.get("kind") or ""), el)))
    kept, size, cut = [], 0, False
    for r, line in reversed(lines):
        size += len(line) + 1
        if size > NOTE_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS and kept:
            cut = True
            break
        kept.append((r, line))
    kept.reverse()
    head = ["[earlier turns of this session left out]"] if cut else []
    return "\n".join(head + [line for _, line in kept])


def said_line(kind, final, el):
    """A participant turn as one line, or None: the person's words, a peer's,
    the model's final answer without its block. Tool rounds, advice and interim
    sentences are context, not what was said."""
    if kind in ("user", "peer") or (kind == "assistant" and int(final or 0) == 1):
        line = transcript_line(kind, el)
        return line if line.split(":", 1)[-1].strip() else None
    return None


def newest_rounds(wall, n):
    """The rows of the newest `n` rounds (one `session_id` + `turn_id`
    each), in wall order."""
    ordered = sorted(wall, key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0))
    keys = []
    for r in ordered:
        k = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
        if k in keys:
            keys.remove(k)
        keys.append(k)
    keep = set(keys[-n:]) if n > 0 else set()
    return [r for r in ordered
            if (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or "")) in keep]


def _cut_tail(text, room):
    if room <= 0:
        return ""
    if len(text) <= room:
        return text
    return text[:max(0, room - 2)].rstrip() + " …"


def _cut_head(text, room):
    if room <= 0:
        return ""
    if len(text) <= room:
        return text
    return "… " + text[len(text) - max(0, room - 2):].lstrip()


def handover_text(pins=(), commitments=(), topic="", summary="", turns=(), limit=3000,
                  summary_title=NOTE_TITLE, taken_out=None):
    """The block, at most `limit` characters, cut by rank (review focus 5):
    pins and open commitments first, then the topic, then the latest turns,
    the summary last. A list keeps whole items as long as it can; the turns
    drop their oldest line first; the summary is cut at its end. The reading
    order is topic, pins, commitments, summary, turns. Pure: no I/O. A dict
    handed as `taken_out` gets the sections that made it into the block: a
    source cut away entirely is no source of its audience (GH #925)."""
    SEP = "\n\n"
    budget = [max(0, int(limit))]
    taken = {} if taken_out is None else taken_out

    def room():
        # Every section after the first costs a separator.
        return budget[0] - (len(SEP) if taken else 0)

    def take(name, text):
        if text:
            budget[0] -= len(text) + (len(SEP) if taken else 0)
            taken[name] = text

    def a_list(name, title, items):
        items = [i for i in items if i]
        if not items:
            return
        head = title + "\n"
        lines = []
        for item in items:
            line = "- " + item
            trial = head + "\n".join(lines + [line])
            if len(trial) <= room():
                lines.append(line)
                continue
            if not lines:
                cut = _cut_tail(line, room() - len(head))
                if len(cut) > 2:
                    lines.append(cut)
            break
        if lines:
            take(name, head + "\n".join(lines))

    a_list("pins", "Pinned:", list(pins))
    a_list("commitments", "Open commitments:", list(commitments))
    if topic:
        head = "The topic still open: "
        text = head + _cut_tail(topic, TOPIC_CHARS)
        if len(text) > room():
            text = _cut_tail(text, room())
        if len(text) > len(head):
            take("topic", text)
    turns = [t for t in turns if t]
    if turns:
        head = "The latest turns:\n"
        kept = list(turns)
        while kept and len(head + "\n".join(kept)) > room():
            if len(kept) == 1:
                kept = [_cut_head(kept[0], room() - len(head))]
                break
            kept.pop(0)
        if kept and kept[0]:
            take("turns", head + "\n".join(kept))
    if summary:
        head = summary_title + "\n"
        text = head + summary
        if len(text) > room():
            text = head + _cut_tail(summary, room() - len(head))
        if len(text) > len(head) + 2:
            take("summary", text)
    return SEP.join(taken[k] for k in ("topic", "pins", "commitments", "summary", "turns")
                    if k in taken)


def pin_lists(pin_rows, blocks, as_of_ms):
    """(pins, commitments): the texts of the valid pins, oldest first, the
    open commitments (`source` `commitment`) apart."""
    pins, commitments = [], []
    for r in sorted(pin_rows, key=lambda r: str(r.get("at") or "")):
        if not pin_valid(r, as_of_ms):
            continue
        text = text_of(blocks.get(str(r.get("hash") or "")))
        if not text:
            continue
        (commitments if str(r.get("source") or "") == COMMITMENT else pins).append(text)
    return pins, commitments


# =================================================================== READS
def gated(cid, table, columns, where, order, limit, session):
    """A read of rows for this step's round: the store hands back only the
    rows the round may see (`round_where`, GH #932), so a limit counts
    visible rows alone. No op at all when nothing may be read (None) -- the
    read's rows are then empty and no store call is made. `session` None is
    a table without `session_id` (`summaries`, `pins`): a round-less read
    there takes nothing, as the gate let nothing through there before."""
    rw = round_where(ROUND, session)
    if rw is None:
        return []
    return [(cid, sel(table, columns, dict(where or {}, **rw), order, limit))]


def base_reads(flow, key):
    """The reads every step of a flow repeats, so that the step that composes
    has them all in ONE answer. Every read whose rows reach a model or a leaf
    carries `audience_set` (GH #925) and asks the store for the rows of this
    round only (GH #932); the gate on the answer stays the second line.
    `key` is the session the flow serves -- for a renewal, its running
    session. Bookkeeping stays ungated: the session's own rows of the `new`
    flow (`r-wallb`: is it new?), the `handover` marks of a close (is it
    prepared already? -- a mark hidden from this round must still stop a
    second note), and the `state` keys."""
    pins = gated("r-pins", "pins", ["hash", "source", "until", "at", "audience_set"],
                 None, None, None, None)
    topic = gated("r-topic", "marks", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "value", "audience_set"],
                  {"kind": "topic"}, [("seq", "desc")], TOPIC_MARKS, key)
    if flow == "close":
        # The note is the session's words and nothing else: pins and the topic
        # are read fresh where the note is used.
        return (gated("r-wall", "wall", ["seq", "turn_id", "kind", "hash", "final", "at",
                                         "audience_set"],
                      {"session_id": key}, [("seq", "asc")], None, key)
                + [("r-marks", sel("marks", ["seq", "session_id", "value"],
                                   {"kind": "handover"}, [("seq", "desc")], HANDOVER_MARKS)),
                   ("r-pend", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                  {"key": "pending:handover:" + key}))])
    if flow == "new":
        # The leaf and its audience as they stand are not read: the flow puts
        # them whole, whatever stands (review Abschluss I-1).
        return ([("r-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": "handover_for"}))]
                + gated("r-marks", "marks", ["seq", "session_id", "value", "at", "audience_set"],
                        {"kind": "handover"}, [("seq", "desc")], HANDOVER_MARKS, key)
                + [("r-wallb", sel("wall", ["turn_id"], {"session_id": key}))]
                + topic)
    # renew
    return (gated("r-sum", "summaries", ["id", "covers_to_seq", "hash", "audience_set"], None,
                  [("covers_to_seq", "desc")], RENEW_SUMMARIES, None)
            + gated("r-wall", "wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind", "hash", "final",
                                       "audience_set"],
                    None, [("seq", "desc")], RENEW_WALL_ROWS, key)
            + pins + topic)


def more_reads(want_hashes):
    """What the answer so far says still has to be read: the blocks of every
    hash the data names."""
    ops = []
    want = sorted(h for h in want_hashes if h)
    if want:
        ops.append(("b-" + short(",".join(want)),
                    sel("blocks", ["hash", "kind", "body"], {"hash": {"in": want}})))
    return ops


def missing(lg, ops):
    return [cid for cid, _ in ops if cid not in lg]


def blocks_of(lg):
    out = {}
    for cid in lg:
        if cid.startswith("b-"):
            for r in rows(lg, cid):
                out.setdefault(str(r.get("hash") or ""), r)
    return out


def prepared_marks(lg):
    out = []
    for r in rows(lg, "r-marks"):
        v = loads(str(r.get("value") or ""), {})
        if v.get("state") == "prepared" and v.get("hash"):
            out.append(dict(r, parsed=v))
    return out


# ======================================================================= LANES
# The round of the message this step serves, read anew in every step (GH #925,
# OR-BD.A.1): this hive's edges touch only `cur_*`, so the round a lane brought
# rides every ledger round trip of its flow -- and the lane's first bundle
# already asks the store for that round's rows (GH #932).
ROUND = ctx.get("audience_set")
lane = str(hop.get("route") or "")
phase = str(ctx.get("cur_phase") or "")
op = str(hop.get("operation") or "")

if lane == "in_close":
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "")
    if not session:
        park("in_close without a session id -- dropped")
    if session in _MEM["prepared"]:
        park("session %s is prepared already -- dropped" % session)
    emit([lstore(base_reads("close", session), "close", session, "")])

if lane == "in_summary":
    session = str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
    text = ""
    for m in d.get("messages") or []:
        if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("origin") == "assistant" and m.get("type") == "text":
            text = str(m.get("text") or "")
            break
    finish = str(hop.get("finish_reason") or "")
    failure = ""
    if finish != "stop":
        failure = "finish_reason %s %s" % (finish or "?", str(hop.get("error_code") or ""))
    elif not text.strip():
        failure = "an empty note"
    if failure or not session:
        # The session stays unprepared, and the next session starts with the
        # block put together without a model.
        park("the handover note of session %s failed: %s" % (session or "?", failure.strip()))
    payload = canonical({"text": text.strip(), "model": str(hop.get("model") or "")})
    key = "pending:handover:" + session
    ops = [("p-clear", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state", "where": {"key": key}}),
           ("p-put", ins("state", {"key": key, "value": payload}))]
    emit([lstore(ops + base_reads("close", session), "note", session, "")])

if lane == "handover":
    # From `./policy`: the first call of a session it did not serve last.
    session = str(hop.get("session_id") or "")
    call = str(hop.get("curator_call") or ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
    turn = str(hop.get("turn_id") or "")
    if not call:
        park("handover without the call it holds -- dropped")
    emit([lstore(base_reads("new", session), "new",
                 call, canonical({"session": session, "turn": turn}))])

if lane == "in_renewed":
    call_id = str(hop.get("call_id") or ctx.get("call_id") or "")
    n = str(hop.get("renewal_n") if hop.get("renewal_n") is not None else "")
    if not call_id:
        park("in_renewed without a call_id -- the block would reach nobody, dropped")
    # The running session of the renewal (the same rule as phase `renew`): a
    # round-less renewal reads that session's rows only (GH #932).
    emit([lstore(base_reads("renew", str(ctx.get("session_id") or call_id)),
                 "renew", call_id, n)])

if lane:
    park("unknown lane %r -- dropped" % lane)

# ================================================================== PHASES
if not op:
    park("a message with neither a lane nor a store answer -- dropped")

lg = legs(d)
call = str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
reason = str(ctx.get("cur_reason") or "")

if phase == "done":
    report_errors(lg)
    emit([])

as_of = now_ms()

if phase in ("close", "note"):
    session = call
    wall = rows(lg, "r-wall")
    said = [r for r in wall if said_line(str(r.get("kind") or ""), r.get("final"),
                                         {"text": "x"}) is not None]
    if not said:
        park("session %s closed without a turn -- no handover" % session)
    if any(str((m.get("parsed") or {}).get("from_session") or "") == session
           for m in prepared_marks(lg)):
        _MEM["prepared"].add(session)
        park("session %s is prepared already -- dropped" % session)
    pend = loads(str((rows(lg, "r-pend") or [{}])[0].get("value") or ""), {})
    if phase == "close":
        # Step 1: the session's words, for the note.
        ops = base_reads("close", session) + more_reads({str(r.get("hash") or "")
                                                         for r in wall})
        if missing(lg, ops):
            emit([lstore(ops, phase, session, "")])
        text = transcript(wall, blocks_of(lg))
        emit([{"header": {"route": "summarize"},
               "system": {"instructions": {"text": HANDOVER_PROMPT % HANDOVER_CHARS}},
               "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": text}]}])
    # Step 2 (`note`): the note is parked; keep it, cut at `handover_chars`.
    # Pins and the topic are not frozen into it: the leaf takes them fresh
    # when the next session starts (review M-6).
    if not pend.get("text"):
        park("the note of session %s is gone -- dropped" % session)
    text = _cut_tail(str(pend.get("text") or "").strip(), HANDOVER_CHARS)
    stamp = now()
    el = {"type": "summary", "text": text}
    h = block_hash(el)
    ops = base_reads("close", session)
    check = ("x-" + h[:12], sel("blocks", ["hash"], {"hash": h}))
    if missing(lg, ops + [check]):
        emit([lstore(ops + [check], phase, session, "")])
    # The note is made of the rows the summarizer was shown, so it may reach no
    # round wider than any of them: the meet of their audiences, NULL when one
    # of them has none -- then the note reaches no round at all (OR-BD-5). The
    # meet runs over EVERY row of the session this step reads, not over this
    # step's transcript (contract review M-5): a row that lands while the
    # summarizer runs shifts the transcript's window past the oldest row it
    # was shown (race driver: a note of an {a,e} row came out {a,b,e}). The
    # wall only grows, so these rows hold every row step 1 showed; a long
    # session's note may come out narrower than its tail, never wider.
    audience = meet_of_rows([r.get("audience_set") for r in wall])
    ops = []
    if not rows(lg, check[0]):
        ops.append(("w-block", ins("blocks", {"hash": h, "kind": "summary", "chars": len(text),
                                              "body": canonical(el), "first_seen": stamp})))
    value = canonical({"state": "prepared", "hash": h, "from_session": session,
                       "sources": [str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in wall],
                       "model": str(pend.get("model") or ""), "chars": len(text)})
    # A meet that comes out None is NOT "no round" but "not decidable" (a
    # source from before the rule): the mark keeps the column NULL and reaches
    # no round, never `[]` (PP-BD-12 covers round-less rows only).
    mark = {"seq": next_seq(), "session_id": session, "turn_id": "",
            "kind": "handover", "value": value, "at": stamp}
    if audience is not None:
        mark["audience_set"] = audience
    ops += [("w-mark", ins("marks", mark)),
            ("w-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                        "where": {"key": "pending:handover:" + session}})]
    _MEM["prepared"].add(session)
    emit([lstore(ops, "done", session, "")])

if phase == "new":
    info = loads(reason, {})
    session = str(info.get("session") or "")
    turn = str(info.get("turn") or "")
    state_rows = rows(lg, "r-state")
    state = {str(r.get("key") or ""): str(r.get("value") or "") for r in state_rows}
    last = state.get("handover_for", "")
    # NEW means: no wall row of this session outside the round now running.
    fresh = all(str(r.get("turn_id") or "") == turn for r in rows(lg, "r-wallb"))
    # The round that receives decides (GH #925): the new session's. Its gate
    # holds every source of the leaf -- the note of the session served last,
    # the topic of any session -- and what it hides leaves no trace.
    prepared = [m for m in prepared_marks(lg)
                if str(m["parsed"].get("from_session") or "") == last and last != session
                and passes(m, ROUND, session)]
    topic, topic_mark = open_topic([m for m in rows(lg, "r-topic")
                                    if passes(m, ROUND, session)])
    want = set()
    if prepared:
        want.add(str(prepared[0]["parsed"].get("hash") or ""))
    ops = base_reads("new", session) + more_reads(want)
    if fresh and missing(lg, ops):
        emit([lstore(ops, "new", call, reason)])
    blocks = blocks_of(lg)
    stamp = now()
    text, audience = "", None
    if fresh:
        # The note of the session served last, when it closed and left one,
        # and the topic still open -- no pins: the window shows them already.
        note, at = "", "not closed"
        if prepared:
            m = prepared[0]
            note = text_of(blocks.get(str(m["parsed"].get("hash") or "")))
            at = str(m.get("at") or "?") if note else at
        taken = {}
        body = handover_text((), (), topic, note, (), HANDOVER_CHARS, taken_out=taken)
        # The leaf's audience is the meet of the sources that made it into it
        # AND of the round that chose them (review R2-I-3), and its head names
        # the session whose words it carries -- the one served last when its
        # note is there, else the topic's -- so it names no session the round
        # sees nothing of (GH #925). The note and the topic were chosen under
        # THIS round: a wider round that joins later would see the leaf only
        # as long as no newer `end` or note it may not see stood in the way
        # (driver: {e,a,b} saw the {e,a} flow's topic exactly when no {e,a}
        # `end` mark was newer) -- so the leaf reaches no round wider than
        # the one it was made for.
        sources, named = [], ""
        if "topic" in taken:
            sources.append(topic_mark.get("audience_set"))
            named = str(topic_mark.get("session_id") or "")
        if "summary" in taken:
            sources.append(prepared[0].get("audience_set"))
            named = last
        else:
            at = "not closed"
        if body:
            text = LEAF_HEAD % (named or "-", at) + "\n" + body
            audience = meet_of_rows(sources + [ROUND])
    writes = []
    if fresh:
        # The leaf, its audience and `handover_for` are PUT whole -- delete +
        # insert in this one bundle, whatever stands -- never "update where it
        # differs from what was read" (review Abschluss I-1): what was read is
        # a round trip old when this bundle lands, and two `new` flows of two
        # rounds overlap. Written only where it differed, the flow that landed
        # last left its own slot under the other's audience, and two flows
        # that both read nothing left two rows per key -- the race driver,
        # every interleaving of two flows in 9 setups (265): 94 views of a
        # leaf by a round one of its sources does not reach, 92 interleavings
        # with doubled or stale rows at rest. Put whole, the bundle that lands
        # last leaves its own leaf, audience and `handover_for` and nothing
        # else (0 and 0). Bound to the hash but written only where it
        # differed, no view leaks either, yet 82 of the 265 end with doubled
        # rows or the session served last without its own leaf.
        writes.append(("w-unslot", {"operation": "delete", "table": "slots",
                                    "where": {"path": LEAF_PATH, "owner": "curator"}}))
        held = ""
        if text:
            leaf = {"path": LEAF_PATH, "text": text}
            h = block_hash(leaf)
            check = ("x-" + h[:12], sel("blocks", ["hash"], {"hash": h}))
            if check[0] not in lg:
                emit([lstore(ops + [check], "new", call, reason)])
            if not rows(lg, check[0]):
                writes.append(("w-block", ins("blocks", {"hash": h, "kind": "system",
                                                         "chars": len(text),
                                                         "body": canonical(leaf),
                                                         "first_seen": stamp})))
            writes.append(("w-slot", ins("slots", {"path": LEAF_PATH, "hash": h,
                                                   "owner": "curator", "at": stamp})))
            # The mark names the session whose note is IN the leaf, else none
            # (review Abschluss m-7): a note the round may not see, or one cut
            # away, leaves no name of its session behind.
            writes.append(("w-mark", ins("marks", with_audience({
                "seq": next_seq(), "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn, "kind": "handover",
                "value": canonical({"state": "set", "hash": h,
                                    "from_session": last if "summary" in taken else "",
                                    "prepared": bool(prepared), "chars": len(text)}),
                "at": stamp}, audience_of(ROUND)))))
            # The audience names the leaf it was made for -- canonical
            # `{"audience", "hash"}`, `hash` the slot's -- and `./policy` shows
            # the leaf to a call only when the hash is the slot's AND the
            # call's round passes the audience, so it falls away when someone
            # joins the session later (GH #925), and a stand mixed of two
            # flows (a failed leg, a row from before) shows nothing (I-1).
            held = canonical({"audience": audience, "hash": h})
        # A new session with nothing to hand over drops the leaf of the last
        # (`w-unslot` above) and its audience: `held` stays "".
        writes += [("w-unaud", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                                "where": {"key": "handover_audience"}}),
                   ("w-aud", ins("state", {"key": "handover_audience", "value": held}))]
    writes += [("w-unfor", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                            "where": {"key": "handover_for"}}),
               ("w-for", ins("state", {"key": "handover_for", "value": session}))]
    # Back to `./policy` with this cell's writes and nothing else (review
    # I-1): the reads the call is built from -- the plan's cover, the rows it
    # holds, the slots with the leaf among them, the pins -- are `./policy`'s
    # own, and it makes them once this bundle is written. `handover` as the
    # reason is what keeps it from sending the same call here twice.
    emit([lstore(writes, "handover-done", call, "handover", POLICY)])

if phase == "renew":
    call_id, n = call, reason
    # The running session of a renewal: the one its context names, else the
    # call itself -- the key the renewal's own mark is written under. It only
    # decides a round-less renewal, which keeps to that session (OR-BD-4).
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or call_id)
    # Every source of the block passes the renewal's round (GH #925): the
    # newest summary it may see and the cover of THAT summary, the newest
    # rounds among the rows it may see, its pins, its topic.
    sums = [r for r in rows(lg, "r-sum") if passes(r, ROUND, session)]
    summary_row = sums[0] if sums else None
    cover = int((summary_row or {}).get("covers_to_seq") or 0)
    wall = [r for r in rows(lg, "r-wall")
            if int(r.get("seq") or 0) > cover and passes(r, ROUND, session)]
    recent = newest_rounds(wall, RENEW_ROUNDS)
    pin_rows = [r for r in rows(lg, "r-pins") if passes(r, ROUND, session)]
    topic, _ = open_topic([m for m in rows(lg, "r-topic") if passes(m, ROUND, session)])
    want = {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in pin_rows if pin_valid(r, as_of)}
    want |= {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in recent}
    if summary_row:
        want.add(str(summary_row.get("hash") or ""))
    ops = base_reads("renew", session) + more_reads(want)
    if missing(lg, ops):
        emit([lstore(ops, "renew", call_id, n)])
    blocks = blocks_of(lg)
    pins, commitments = pin_lists(pin_rows, blocks, as_of)
    turns = []
    for r in recent:
        el = element_of(blocks.get(str(r.get("hash") or "")))
        line = said_line(str(r.get("kind") or ""), r.get("final"), el) if el else None
        if line:
            turns.append(line)
    summary = text_of(blocks.get(str((summary_row or {}).get("hash") or "")))
    body = handover_text(pins, commitments, topic, summary, turns,
                         HANDOVER_CHARS, "Earlier in this conversation, summarised:")
    text = without_ids(RENEW_HEAD + ("\n" + body if body else ""))
    stamp = now()
    el = {"type": "summary", "text": text}
    h = block_hash(el)
    check = ("x-" + h[:12], sel("blocks", ["hash"], {"hash": h}))
    if check[0] not in lg:
        emit([lstore(ops + [check], "renew", call_id, n)])
    writes = []
    if not rows(lg, check[0]):
        writes.append(("w-block", ins("blocks", {"hash": h, "kind": "summary", "chars": len(text),
                                                 "body": canonical(el), "first_seen": stamp})))
    writes.append(("w-mark", ins("marks", with_audience({
        "seq": next_seq(), "session_id": call_id, "turn_id": "", "kind": "handover",
        "value": canonical({"state": "renewed", "hash": h, "call_id": call_id, "renewal_n": n,
                            "chars": len(text)}),
        "at": stamp}, audience_of(ROUND)))))
    # Which renewal the call stands at (GH #935): `./policy` takes a fresh
    # snapshot of the full identity when this differs from the one it holds,
    # so a renewed session starts on the identity as it is now. One key PER
    # SESSION (review I-4): a hive-wide key moved the snapshot of every other
    # session -- of another round too -- at the moment this one renewed, a
    # timing channel and a cache break they never caused. PUT whole --
    # delete + insert, like `handover_for` -- so two renewals that overlap
    # leave one row, the one that landed last.
    ren_key = "renewed_last:" + session
    writes += [("w-unren", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                            "where": {"key": ren_key}}),
               ("w-ren", ins("state", {"key": ren_key,
                                       "value": canonical({"call_id": call_id, "n": n,
                                                           "hash": h})}))]
    try:
        renewal_n = int(n)
    except ValueError:
        renewal_n = n
    # The splitter's section shape (the words under `payload`), so the member's
    # advise edge and the channel read it like any `context` section.
    advise = {"header": {"route": "sidecar", "section": "context", "call_id": call_id,
                         "renewal_n": renewal_n},
              "messages": [], "section": "context", "payload": text}
    emit([advise, lstore(writes, "done", call_id, n)])

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

handover_chars.description: The longest handover block, in characters, without its one-line head. What does not fit is cut by rank: pins and open commitments first, then the topic, then the latest turns, the summary last. The leaf of a new session carries the note and the topic; a renewed live session's block carries all of them.

renew_rounds.description: How many of the newest rounds (one session and turn each) a renewed live session is told as text, beside the summary, the pins and the topic.

description.purpose: What one session leaves for the next, and what a renewed live session of the same call needs to carry on (GH #896). When a session closes, `./summarizer` writes a handover note off the hot path, kept as a block of kind `summary` with a `marks` row `handover` (state `prepared`). On the first call of a NEW session `./policy` hands the call here once: the system leaf `history.handover` is set -- the note of the session served last and the topic still open, as far as the new session's round may see them, put together without a model, with their audience -- never wider than that round -- bound to the leaf's hash in `state` `handover_audience` (GH #925) -- and the call goes back to `./policy`, which reads its window itself. When a duplex session of a running call was renewed, the running conversation is put together without a model and leaves as a `sidecar` section `context` that carries `renewal_n` and `call_id`.
description.not_in_scope: No wall writes and no window: `./intake` writes the wall and `./policy` builds the window. No model of its own: the note goes through `./summarizer`, the one model door of the hive. The pack family `handover` belongs to the identity pusher and is never touched here; this cell's leaf is `history.handover`.
description.emits_meaning: lstore: ledger reads and writes; once per new session the last bundle answers to `./policy` (phase `handover-done`, reason `handover`) with this cell's writes only. summarize: the handover note request for `./summarizer`. sidecar: the block for a renewed live session, section `context`, its words under `payload`.
description.consumes_meaning: in_close (a closed session), handover (from `./policy`: the first call of a session it did not serve last), in_renewed (a renewed duplex session: `call_id`, `renewal_n`), in_summary (the note), and the ledger's answers to its own steps.
